# Choosing a play

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-play-guide.ts. Edit packages/plays/src/descriptions.ts. -->

Choose by buyer situation. Set your founder profile and product positioning in Setup. Email needs a deliverable address and configured sender; other channels need their corresponding contact details. Preview drafts before sending.

The dashboard shows current cadence timing and optional direct mail. Live API runs can send; manual channels require you to post and confirm. Outputs below describe outreach, not completed sales outcomes.

## show-hn

- **When to use it:** A founder has launched something relevant on Show HN.
- **What it does:** Drafts a contextual email and sends it when run live; it does not post on HN.
- **What you need:** Founder contact, launch URL and a specific observation from the launch.
- **What it produces:** An email draft, with a recorded send when dispatched.

## job-change

- **When to use it:** A buyer has moved into a role where your product could help.
- **What it does:** Drafts outreach about their new responsibilities and runs the configured follow-ups.
- **What you need:** Contact, new role and company, plus your concrete product advantage.
- **What it produces:** An email draft, recorded sends and a follow-up cadence.

## post-funding

- **When to use it:** A relevant company has announced funding and may be changing priorities.
- **What it does:** Drafts funding-context outreach and sends email with the configured follow-ups.
- **What you need:** Buyer contact, company, round, amount and announcement source.
- **What it produces:** An email draft, recorded sends and a follow-up cadence.

## accelerator-batch

- **When to use it:** Your buyers are building companies in an accelerator cohort.
- **What it does:** Drafts cohort-context email and runs the configured follow-ups without implying you share their affiliation.
- **What you need:** Founder contact, company, cohort and a specific useful observation or offer.
- **What it produces:** Personalized email drafts and recorded cadence activity.

## concierge

- **When to use it:** A new signup needs guided onboarding.
- **What it does:** Runs an automated voice call, with optional preparation and summary emails.
- **What you need:** Name, email, phone and onboarding context; a call window is optional.
- **What it produces:** Call results, email drafts and receipts for dispatched actions.

## demo-no-show

- **When to use it:** A prospect missed an already scheduled demo.
- **What it does:** Sends a recovery email and, when a phone is supplied, an SMS; schedules the follow-up.
- **What you need:** Contact, company, missed-demo time and a real rescheduling link.
- **What it produces:** Recovery message drafts, recorded sends and a follow-up cadence.

## competitor-switch

- **When to use it:** A buyer has a relevant connection to a competing product.
- **What it does:** Drafts an honest switching pitch from available evidence and sends email with configured follow-ups.
- **What you need:** Contact, company, competitor and a specific supported advantage; usage claims need evidence.
- **What it produces:** A migration-focused draft and recorded outreach activity.

## stack-consolidation

- **When to use it:** A repository integrates several vendors your product could consolidate.
- **What it does:** Drafts email about reducing integration work and runs configured follow-ups.
- **What you need:** Contact, detected vendor stack and a concrete consolidation advantage.
- **What it produces:** A stack-specific email draft and recorded outreach activity.

## repo-interest

- **When to use it:** Someone stars an adjacent repository relevant to your product.
- **What it does:** Drafts a complementary introduction, then sends email with configured follow-ups.
- **What you need:** Contact, starred repository and a factual connection to what you offer.
- **What it produces:** An interest-based email draft and recorded outreach activity.

## luma-events

- **When to use it:** An upcoming event overlaps with your buyers and location.
- **What it does:** Drafts event-context outreach to public hosts or guests and sends through the configured motion.
- **What you need:** Contact, event title, date, location, URL and your relevant offer.
- **What it produces:** An event-specific draft and recorded outreach; stale events are held for review.

## hiring-signal

- **When to use it:** An open role reveals work your product could help a company perform.
- **What it does:** Researches the job context, drafts email to the hiring owner and runs configured follow-ups.
- **What you need:** Contact, company, job title or posting, and your supported ramp-time claim.
- **What it produces:** A hiring-context draft and recorded outreach activity.

## podcast-guest

- **When to use it:** A podcast guest described a problem relevant to your work.
- **What it does:** Drafts and sends a one-touch email anchored to a specific episode moment.
- **What you need:** Guest contact, podcast, episode and an exact quotation or timestamped observation.
- **What it produces:** An episode-specific email draft and recorded outreach activity.

## breakup-revive

- **When to use it:** An eligible past conversation has gone quiet for the selected cold window.
- **What it does:** Reads prior ledger activity and drafts a fresh email to reopen the conversation.
- **What you need:** An existing contact with outreach history; not-a-fit and do-not-contact stops stay excluded.
- **What it produces:** A revival draft and a recorded send when dispatched.

## profile-intro

- **When to use it:** You have identified a person directly rather than through a timed signal.
- **What it does:** Uses Add Prospect research to draft an introduction on the selected channel.
- **What you need:** A LinkedIn or X profile, founder positioning and a reachable channel.
- **What it produces:** A queue row and introduction draft; API channels send, while X is posted manually.

## x-repost-intro

- **When to use it:** A potential product user reposts or quotes an account you watch.
- **What it does:** Uses the repost and buyer context to draft an adoption introduction with configured follow-ups.
- **What you need:** A watched account, repost evidence, buyer fit and reachable contact.
- **What it produces:** An outreach draft and recorded activity on the selected channel; X sends are manual.

## x-amplify

- **When to use it:** A relevant account could share your launch and has a reachable email.
- **What it does:** Drafts and sends a one-touch email asking for amplification, grounded in their repost.
- **What you need:** Contact, X handle and repost evidence; supply a launch date only when known.
- **What it produces:** An amplification email draft and a recorded send.

## x-amplify-dm

- **When to use it:** You want to approach an amplifier directly on X.
- **What it does:** Drafts a DM or public reply for you to copy and send by hand.
- **What you need:** X handle, repost evidence and DM availability; no email is needed.
- **What it produces:** A manual message draft; Mark sent records your confirmed activity.

## sources-sought

- **When to use it:** An agency is gathering capabilities before a procurement.
- **What it does:** Drafts an email answering a Sources Sought or Presolicitation notice and follows the configured cadence.
- **What you need:** Published contact, agency, notice details and a supported fit to the requirement.
- **What it produces:** A notice-specific outreach draft and recorded sends, not a submitted bid.

## civic-pilot

- **When to use it:** A city or county agenda identifies a need suited to a small pilot.
- **What it does:** Drafts email connecting the agenda item to a feasible pilot and runs configured follow-ups.
- **What you need:** Contact, municipality, agenda item, meeting date, your advantage and a purchasing vehicle or threshold.
- **What it produces:** A pilot outreach draft and recorded sends, not a procurement approval.

## design-partner-loi

- **When to use it:** An enterprise, government or hardware buyer could help shape a scoped pilot.
- **What it does:** Drafts email that progresses from problem ownership toward a design-partner discussion and pilot.
- **What you need:** Contact, company, eligible buyer type and your specific product advantage.
- **What it produces:** Drafts and recorded cadence activity, not a signed letter of intent.

## discovery-interview

- **When to use it:** You need to learn how an owner-operator handles a specific problem.
- **What it does:** Drafts a learning-focused email and runs configured follow-ups.
- **What you need:** Contact, business, business type and the concrete topic you want to understand.
- **What it produces:** Interview-request drafts and recorded outreach, not completed interviews.

## free-pilot

- **When to use it:** You can offer an owner-operator a concrete, small piece of work for free.
- **What it does:** Drafts a practical pilot offer and sends email with configured follow-ups.
- **What you need:** Contact, business type and exactly what you will set up for them.
- **What it produces:** Pilot-offer drafts and recorded outreach; delivery of the pilot remains yours.

## new-business

- **When to use it:** A recently licensed or registered business has an immediate setup need.
- **What it does:** Drafts email tied to the opening signal and runs configured follow-ups.
- **What you need:** Contact, business type, license type, recency and your concrete offer.
- **What it produces:** Opening-context drafts and recorded outreach activity.

## community-reply

- **When to use it:** Someone publicly asks for recommendations, compares tools or seeks a replacement.
- **What it does:** Drafts a helpful Reddit or HN reply with your affiliation for you to post by hand.
- **What you need:** Thread evidence, author handle and your verified product brief; no email needed.
- **What it produces:** A public-reply draft; Mark posted records your confirmation without starting a cadence.
